rows.title: Ireland Finds U.S. Tourists During Pandemic May Be Trouble. But So Is Their Absence
rows.standfirst: There's a perception that Americans are resistant to wearing masks and are refusing to self-isolate for 14 days upon arrival. Still, one hotel workers says, "We are missing the Americans greatly."

rows.title: Jobs, Labor And The 1936 GM Strike
rows.standfirst: The brutal unemployment situation in the US today is making a lot of people think again about labor unions. Which had their first major victory after a 1936 strike.

rows.title: Mask Communication
rows.standfirst: Why won't some people wear masks? Is there anything we can do to convince them? We look to behavioral economics for help. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Families Stuck At Home Turn To Board Game Catan, Sending Sales Skyrocketing
rows.standfirst: It's a strategy game of trade and development, and it has become a hit as people shelter at home during the pandemic. The German founder of the board game describes how he came up with Catan.

rows.title: Long Road To Recovery: Hiring Slows In July, As U.S. Employers Add 1.8 Million Jobs
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 1.8 million jobs in July, down from 4.8 million the month before. The unemployment rate inched down to 10.2%.

rows.title: Trump Signs Executive Order That Will Effectively Ban Use Of TikTok In the U.S.
rows.standfirst: The president also issued an executive order aimed at cutting ties between the U.S. and the owner of the popular Chinese communications and social media app WeChat.

rows.title: One Drug, Two Prices
rows.standfirst: Faced with the prospect of paying for an expensive drug to treat his daughter, this dad found a nearly identical product for thousands of dollars less. But the insurance company wouldn't let him.

rows.title: Prices For COVID-19 Vaccines Are Starting To Come Into Focus
rows.standfirst: Moderna, one of the leading horses in the coronavirus vaccine race, has already made deals at between $32 and $37 a dose for some foreign countries. The U.S. price is expected to be lower.

rows.title: With $600 Unemployment Aid Gone, Homelessness Is What Keeps This Mother Up At Night
rows.standfirst: Sandy Villatoro, a housekeeper who lost her job in March, doesn't know how she'll pay the bills for her family of four now that the additional $600 weekly in federal aid she was receiving has expired.

rows.title: 'Fresh Air' Remembers Veteran Journalist Pete Hamill
rows.standfirst: Hamill, who died Aug. 5, was a columnist and editor at the New York Post and the New York Daily News, covering wars, crime and the people of NYC's boroughs. Originally broadcast in '94, '08 and '11.

rows.title: U.S. Economy On High Alert Over Shaky Future Of Extra Jobless Benefits
rows.standfirst: As Congress debates whether to renew supplemental unemployment benefits for people thrown out of work by the pandemic, new research shows those benefits offer a critical boost for the U.S. economy.

rows.title: Twitter, Facebook Remove Trump Post Over False Claim About Children And COVID-19
rows.standfirst: Both social networks said the president's false claims that children are "almost immune" from COVID-19 violated its policy on coronavirus misinformation.

rows.title: Why Your Internet Sucks
rows.standfirst: We answer two questions today: Why is American internet so bad? And why was the unemployment benefit extension set at $600?

rows.title: Facebook Launches Instagram Reels, Hoping To Lure TikTok Users
rows.standfirst: The social network's new Reels feature on Instagram is launching as TikTok faces scrutiny in Washington over its Chinese ownership.

rows.title: 'Nothing Feels Tangible': Virtual Is New Reality For Grads Starting New Jobs
rows.standfirst: Postings for entry-level positions popular with new college grads fell by 73%, compared with before COVID-19 hit. And for those in the class of 2020 who have landed jobs, it's been a strange journey.

rows.title: Trump: TikTok Must Be Sold In 90 Days, Cites 'Credible Evidence' Of Security Threat
rows.standfirst: The move follows a previous executive order from the president that would make "transactions" between U.S. citizens and the Chinese-owned app illegal.

rows.title: Want To Refinance Your Home Loan With Record Low Rates? Get Ready For A Hefty Fee
rows.standfirst: Mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will start charging an extra upfront fee in September ... as much as $1,500 for a $300,000 loan. Lenders are upset and blame the Trump administration.

rows.title: Under Trump, SEC Enforcement Of Insider Trading Dropped To Lowest Point In Decades
rows.standfirst: Kodak and Sen. Richard Burr, R-N.C., are facing high-profile insider trading investigations, but data show the Securities and Exchange Commission pursued far fewer insider trading cases last year.

rows.title: Big Rigged
rows.standfirst: Driving a truck used to mean freedom. Now it means a mountain of debt. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: The Economics of Gods and Mortals
rows.standfirst: The first milestone in the history of economics was an 8th century B.C. poem — a lecture by an ancient Greek poet to his deadbeat brother.

rows.title: Midsummer Shopping In Recovery Mode: July Retail Sales Rise 1.2%
rows.standfirst: People particularly stocked up on electronics and appliances, took more trips with stops at gas stations, and cautiously went out to eat as more stores and restaurants reopened.

rows.title: New California Financial Watchdog Would Take Aim At Predatory Lenders Amid Pandemic
rows.standfirst: California may be on the cusp of creating a watchdog agency. Proponents say federal regulators aren't doing their job, leaving leaving millions of Americans vulnerable during the coronavirus crisis.

rows.title: Fortnite Uses Apple's Own '1984' Ad Against It In Dispute Over Payments
rows.standfirst: Apple pulled the popular shooting game from its App Store, after its developer tried to get around the fee Apple requires from in-app purchases.

rows.title: As Journalists Work From Home, Their Newsrooms Are Shutting Down
rows.standfirst: In closing five of its newsrooms permanently, Tribune Publishing said it saw "no clear path forward in terms of returning to work." But affected unions argued the closures were unnecessary.

rows.title: When $600 Goes Away
rows.standfirst: Millions of jobless Americans are desperate to know whether their unemployment benefits will be extended, and by how much. But Congress just went on vacation.

rows.title: New Jobless Claims Dip Below 1 Million For 1st Time Since March
rows.standfirst: Initial unemployment claims had been above 1 million for 20 straight weeks. The total receiving unemployment also dipped, to 28.3 million, as of July 25.

rows.title: Trump's Methane Rollback That Big Oil Doesn't Want
rows.standfirst: The rule ends Obama-era restrictions on emissions of methane, a potent climate-warming gas. The move could make it harder to argue that natural gas is a cleaner-burning fossil fuel than coal.

rows.title: Top Facebook Official: Our Aim Is To Make Lying On The Platform 'More Difficult'
rows.standfirst: Facebook's head of security policy, Nathaniel Gleicher, said that the company is working harder than ever to counteract efforts to interfere in the 2020 presidential election.

rows.title: Airbnb Sues Guest Whose Sacramento Party Drew Gunfire Injuring 3
rows.standfirst: " This marks the first time Airbnb has taken affirmative steps to initiate legal proceedings against a booking guest for throwing an unauthorized party," the company said.

rows.title: An Immigration Backfire?
rows.standfirst: Limiting high-skilled immigration to the U.S. may not save jobs for Americans; it might even cost jobs.

rows.title: Crisis At The Post Office
rows.standfirst: The United States Postal Service is in the middle of a political firestorm. What happened, and can it be fixed? Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: U.S. Lobster Dealers Hope To Claw Back Market Share In Europe
rows.standfirst: A new trade deal with Europe lifts tariffs that had put U.S. producers at a competitive disadvantage. Lobster shipments worldwide have suffered this year, largely as a result of the coronavirus.

rows.title: Why Do Diamonds Cost More Than Water?
rows.standfirst: The Diamond-Water Paradox: If we need water to survive and we don't need diamonds, why are diamonds expensive and water cheap?

rows.title: Crowdsourced border wall donors disturbed by fraud and money laundering charges
rows.standfirst: Some donors have gotten their money back after contributing to "We Build the Wall." Former Trump adviser Steve Bannon and other officials at the nonprofit are accused of bilking donors.

rows.title: Day Care, Grandparent, Pod Or Nanny? How To Manage The Risks Of Pandemic Child Care
rows.standfirst: At least two-thirds of U.S. families are struggling to find safe and affordable child care as the pandemic rages on. NPR asked infectious disease experts to help sort the health risks of each option.

rows.title: Airbnb Bans All Parties At Its Listings Worldwide, Citing Public Health Mandates
rows.standfirst: Airbnb properties are prohibited from hosting parties or accommodating groups larger than 16 people until further notice. The company said the new policy is "in the best interest of public health."

rows.title: Uber, Lyft Will Not Suspend Service In California After Court Gives Them More Time
rows.standfirst: An appeals court has given the ride-hailing companies more time to fight a judge's order that they reclassify their drivers as employees to comply with state law.

rows.title: The Looming Eviction Crisis
rows.standfirst: Millions of renters in the US are facing the prospect of eviction from their homes.

rows.title: Former Uber Executive Charged With Paying 'Hush Money' To Conceal Massive Breach
rows.standfirst: Federal prosecutors allege Uber's former chief security officer Joe Sullivan covered up the breach and arranged a $100,000 payment to the hackers.

rows.title: As We Return To Work And School During The Pandemic, Can The Air Inside Be Kept Safe?
rows.standfirst: Changes to ventilation — everything from opening windows to making pricey upgrades to HVAC systems — can help reduce the risk of the coronavirus being spread inside a building.

rows.title: There's More Big Tech In Your Life Than You Even Know. Check Out Your Stock Portfolio
rows.standfirst: The market is hitting records, in large part because of a handful of superstar tech stocks. Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, Facebook, Netflix and Google's parent dominate indexes in retirement funds.

rows.title: Braving Your Student Loan Payments: Tips To Pay Off Student Debt
rows.standfirst: The student loan system is confusing. Sometimes it can seem designed to make borrowers fail. But if you know how to navigate it, you're more likely to save money in the long run.

rows.title: How To Tell A Real COVID-19 Contact Tracer's Call From A Scammer's
rows.standfirst: A loved one's health could depend on the truth if you get a call from a real contact tracer about your exposure to the coronavirus. But beware impostors who ask you for payment or to click on a link.

rows.title: Becky, We Hardly Knew Ye
rows.standfirst: We bought a junk bond back in December. Then COVID-19 sent the economy into a tailspin, and the company that issued the junk bond declared bankruptcy. But that wasn't the end of the story.

rows.title: How Feds Decide On Remdesivir Shipments To States Remains Mysterious
rows.standfirst: The federal government is in charge of distributing one of the few treatment options for COVID-19: the antiviral drug remdesivir. But how are decisions made about which states need it most?

rows.title: Zoom Turns Record Profit Thanks To Coronavirus Shutdowns
rows.standfirst: The videoconferencing company is seeing surging demand — and profit — as so much of daily life goes virtual during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: The Inclusion Payoff
rows.standfirst: Women and non-white men are gaining ground when it comes to science and engineering degrees, but not when it comes to patents.

rows.title: Indian Economy Shrinks By 24% As The Country Sees Its Highest Coronavirus Numbers
rows.standfirst: "This year, we are facing an extraordinary situation," Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told a conference last week before GDP figures were released. "We are facing an act of God."

rows.title: United, Delta, American Say They Are Dropping Change Fees For Domestic Flights
rows.standfirst: United's CEO says the change was a top request from customers. Delta and American followed suit after United's announcement. Airlines are trying to coax wary customers to return amid the pandemic.

rows.title: Voice of America Journalists: New CEO Endangers Reporters, Harms U.S. Aims
rows.standfirst: Fourteen Voice of America journalists accused USAGM CEO Michael Pack of imperiling reporters. Pack recently said of VOA, "It's a great place to put a foreign spy."

rows.title: Black Americans Worry Postal Changes Could Disrupt History Of Secure Jobs
rows.standfirst: Starting with a special law after the Civil War, the U.S. Postal Service has provided a path to the middle class for generations of African Americans. Some worry a privatization push threatens that.

rows.title: Mayors Of College Towns Brace For The Economic Impact Of Remote Learning
rows.standfirst: Mayor Walt Maddox of Tuscaloosa, Ala., Mayor Donnie Tuck of Hampton, Va., and Mayor Bruce Teague of Iowa City, Iowa, on how they're trying to halt the spread of the coronavirus.

rows.title: Coffee Keeps Its Mojo: Producers Overcome Pandemic Obstacles
rows.standfirst: Coffee has remained widely available on supermarket shelves even though COVID-19 has been particularly bad in some of the world's largest coffee-growing nations.

rows.title: TikTok Workers Feel 'Anxiety,' 'Anger,' And 'Rage,' Amid Trump Crackdown
rows.standfirst: TikTok employee Patrick Ryan has launched a legal challenge against the Trump administration to protect TikTok workers. The White House has given the popular app an ultimatum: Sell or be banned.

rows.title: An Ode To Taxes
rows.standfirst: Taxes get a bad reputation, but they were central to the formation of representative government and even the written word.

rows.title: Hurricane Laura Losses Include 10 Deaths, Up To $12 Billion
rows.standfirst: Laura is blamed for at least 10 deaths, and it's estimated to have caused anywhere from $4 billion to $12 billion in damages. But officials and experts say the price tag could have been far worse.

rows.title: Rebound In Consumer Spending Fades In July
rows.standfirst: Consumer spending rose 1.9% last month — but the rebound slowed from May and June. Unemployment benefits continued to prop up spending in July, but that may change in August.

rows.title: More Space, Please: Home Sales Booming Despite Pandemic, Recession
rows.standfirst: Despite high unemployment, a severe recession and economic uncertainty, the housing market is on a tear. Sales are booming, and prices hit a record high. Low rates and remote work are driving factors.

rows.title: What A Piece Of Work Is The Post Office
rows.standfirst: The rather Shakespearean situation of the U.S. Postal Service

rows.title: Chemical Fire Burns Near Lake Charles, La., In Aftermath Of Hurricane Laura
rows.standfirst: Smoke is rising over the city from a plant complex that makes chlorine for swimming pools, according to a state official. Residents are advised to shelter in place until further notice.
